shortDescription: Add, modify and delete services within a Consul cluster

options.name: address
options.description: The address to advertise that the service listens on. This value is passed as the C(address) parameter to Consul's C(/v1/agent/service/register) API method, so refer to the Consul API documentation for further details.

options.name: ca_path
options.description: The CA bundle to use for https connections.

options.name: enable_tag_override
options.description: Specifies to disable the anti-entropy feature for this service's tags. If C(EnableTagOverride) is set to true then external agents can update this service in the catalog and modify the tags.

options.name: id
options.description: Specifies a unique ID for this service. This must be unique per agent. This defaults to the O(name) parameter if not provided. If O(state=absent), defaults to the service name if supplied.

options.name: meta
options.description: Optional meta data used for filtering. For keys, the characters C(A-Z), C(a-z), C(0-9), C(_), C(-) are allowed. Not allowed characters are replaced with underscores.

options.name: name
options.description: Unique name for the service on a node, must be unique per node, required if registering a service.

options.name: port
options.description: The port on which the consul agent is running.

options.name: scheme
options.description: The protocol scheme on which the Consul agent is running. Defaults to V(http) and can be set to V(https) for secure connections.

options.name: service_port
options.description: The port on which the service is listening. Can optionally be supplied for registration of a service, that is if O(name) or O(id) is set.

options.name: state
options.description: Whether the service should be present or absent.

options.name: tags
options.description: Tags that are attached to the service registration.

options.name: token
options.description: The token to use for authorization.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Whether to verify the TLS certificate of the Consul agent.
